## Symptom

A full default-selection run (`make test`) fails with ONE test, which passes in isolation:

    FAILED tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py::test_success_telemetry_survives_an_empty_usage_dict
      - StopIteration
      at: line = next(r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records if "llm call [" in r.getMessage())

Isolated: `pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` -> 12 passed. Order-dependent, not a defect
in the test's own subject.

## Proven mechanism (clean tree, no other changes applied)

`src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:120 configure_logging()` does, at lines 145-146:

    lg = logging.getLogger("rebar")
    lg.setLevel(level)
    lg.propagate = False

`propagate = False` on the shared `rebar` parent logger is PROCESS-GLOBAL and is never restored.
pytest's `caplog` captures via a handler on the ROOT logger, so once propagation is off no
`rebar.*` record can reach it again. Every subsequent caplog assertion silently sees zero records.

Reproduced directly on a CLEAN checkout (changes stashed), two tests in one file:

    def test_a_baseline(caplog):                 # PASSES
        with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO): _emit()
        assert any("llm call [" in r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records)

    def test_b_after_configure_logging(caplog):  # FAILS: assert False
        from rebar.review_bot.config import configure_logging
        configure_logging()
        with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO): _emit()
        assert any("llm call [" in r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records)

Result: `1 failed, 1 passed`. The only difference is the `configure_logging()` call.
`caplog.at_level()` does not help - it adjusts levels, not propagation.

Two entry points reach it: `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1288` calls it directly, and
`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:202` calls it at MODULE IMPORT time (so merely importing the app
poisons the process; that path is inert in this checkout only because `fastapi` is absent).

## Why this matters beyond one red test

The failure is silent and non-local: it does not point at `configure_logging`, it points at an
unrelated victim whose position in the run order falls after the poisoning. Any future caplog
assertion on a `rebar.*` logger is one ordering change away from the same mystery, and the
affected assertions provide NO coverage in a full run while appearing green in isolation.

## Suggested direction (not implemented)

`propagate = False` exists to stop double-logging through uvicorn/root in the container. Options:
attach the handler without disabling propagation and rely on the existing marker guard to avoid
duplicates; make the propagation change conditional on actually running under uvicorn; or add an
autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py` that snapshots and restores the `rebar` logger's
`level`/`propagate`/`handlers` around every test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A caplog-based assertion on a `rebar.*` logger still captures records after
      `configure_logging()` has run in the same process, pinned by a test that fails before the fix.
- [x] The double-logging that `propagate=False` was introduced to prevent is still prevented; the
      existing `test_configure_logging_emits_rebar_info_to_stdout` and
      `test_configure_logging_is_idempotent` stay green.
- [x] `make test` (default selection) is green by exit code with no order-dependent failure.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code.
